During operational qualification, commanded steering position shall update at least once per second.

At every epoch in the common E-002 acceptance set, valid heading error shall be at most 10 degrees against an independent reference.

Within 30 seconds after a watchdog reset under E-003 preconditions, restored gate progress shall equal the last persisted gate progress.
After watchdog reset, each active survival, low-energy, recovery and isolation restriction shall remain effective until its own release condition is met.
When conservative usable energy reaches or falls below protected reserve, the vessel shall set the low-energy flag within 5 seconds.

While the low-energy flag is set, autonomous navigation shall remain active.
While the low-energy flag is set, collision-response behavior shall remain active.
After conservative usable energy exceeds 1.2 times protected reserve for 10 continuous minutes, the vessel shall clear the low-energy flag independently of survival/recovery flags.
Payload operation shall remain inhibited whenever a low-energy, survival or recovery restriction is active.
With a functioning link, current position, operating mode and health telemetry delivery intervals shall not exceed 30 seconds.
Through a 24-hour telemetry-link outage, autonomous mission control shall continue without operator intervention.
After link restoration, a current telemetry record shall arrive within the active TelemetryDeliveryCadence interval.
After reconnection, retained backlog records shall be transmitted in ascending acquisition sequence order.
During backlog transfer, current telemetry shall continue to meet TelemetryDeliveryCadence.
In the E-006 injection test, ingress detection shall occur within 60 seconds of injection starting.
In the E-006 test, ingress detection shall set the recovery-request state.
In the E-006 test, the vessel shall remain afloat for the full 30 minutes.
After the E-006 test, enclosed-electronics water-sensitive indicators shall show no liquid ingress.
Throughout the E-006 test with a functioning link, position reporting shall meet the active TelemetryDeliveryCadence.
Periodic mission records shall be acquired at least once per second normally and once per minute in low-energy or survival operation.
Acquired mission records shall remain retrievable onboard for at least 30 days.

Every external-command disposition, reset, motor-enable transition, ingress detection, recovery request, navigation-degraded transition, low-energy flag transition and qualification change shall have an event record regardless of periodic cadence.

Each detected missing sequence of scheduled records shall have a gap indication in retrieved data.
After watchdog reset or abrupt power removal, every record older than 5 seconds before interruption shall remain readable.
Communication reconnection shall not delete retained mission records.
Each disqualifying transition shall be durably stored before its associated commanded intervention or motor enable.
On restart with absent or inconsistent persisted qualification state, the vessel shall adopt nonqualifying status.
In each E-008 campaign, at least 1710 of 1800 scheduled epochs shall contain valid position and heading observations.
Navigation observations older than 5 seconds shall be marked invalid.
When position or heading becomes invalid due to age, the vessel shall enter navigation-degraded state within 1 second.
The controller shall not use observations marked invalid as current navigation inputs.
One adult shall move all mission equipment 100 m without assistance.
Each separately lifted assembly shall have a mass no greater than 15 kg.
One adult shall assemble the vessel from its transport configuration within 30 minutes.
One adult shall pack the vessel into its transport configuration within 30 minutes.
One adult shall launch the assembled vessel without assistance.
One adult shall retrieve the vessel from the water without assistance.
Each P-003 replacement shall take no more than 30 minutes.
Each P-003 replacement shall leave bonded structural joints and adjacent parts intact.
After each P-003 replacement, the assembly shall meet the N-043 immersion criterion.
After each P-003 replacement, affected actuators shall complete their full commanded travel.
The vessel shall acquire and maintain encounter tracks with the reviewed class- and condition-specific timely acquisition and continuity performance required by S-001.
The vessel shall update collision-risk estimates at least once per second.

Missing or geometrically invalid boundaries shall inhibit mission start.
Navigation loss or absence of a feasible maneuver shall produce an explicit degraded-route verdict instead of a safe-route verdict.

Motor restart shall remain inhibited after local isolation until deliberate local reset.
After remote control has been lost for 5 seconds during manual powered recovery, the vessel shall command zero thrust within a further 1 second.
Location reporting shall continue at the active telemetry cadence after remote-control loss whenever a telemetry link is available.

The vessel shall present the shapes prescribed for its current mode by the S-004 compliance matrix without a person aboard.
The vessel shall present the sound signals prescribed for its current mode by the S-004 compliance matrix without a person aboard.
A commanded mode change shall select the corresponding signaling configuration within 1 second.
Each detectable signaling failure shall be logged within 5 seconds of detection.
With a functioning link, each detected signaling failure shall be reported to shore within 5 seconds.
Each deployment shall have a dated compliance record identifying the craft, dimensions, waters, operating modes, applicable navigation and radio obligations, and permission evidence.
Deployment release shall be withheld while any mandatory authorization is absent, expired or unresolved.
The shore endpoint shall display UTC sample time, position, mode, conservative usable energy, reserve, faults and age from each current telemetry record.
The shore endpoint shall indicate stale data when record age exceeds its C-101 mode threshold until receipt of a record within its applicable threshold.
The shore endpoint shall preserve received record identity and sequence numbers across the C-101 outage/reconnection test.
The shore endpoint shall not present a duplicate telemetry record as a new observation.
Commands failing authentication shall cause zero accepted actuator or mission-state changes.
Commands with previously used sequence numbers shall cause zero accepted actuator or mission-state changes.
Commands older than 30 seconds shall cause zero accepted actuator or mission-state changes.

Acceptance of external mission or steering control during a qualifying attempt shall permanently disqualify that attempt.
Navigation shall meet E-002 and E-008 acceptance criteria at visibility of at least 1 km in daylight and darkness.
Traffic assessment shall meet the reviewed class-specific S-001 criteria at visibility of at least 1 km in daylight and darkness.

Full autonomous sailing shall remain inhibited while N-035 resumption eligibility is false.
Every blocked sailing-resumption attempt shall record the blocking condition.
After each N-044 exposure, external mechanisms shall complete their full commanded travel without seizure.
After each N-044 exposure, structural joints shall show no separation or through-cracks on visual inspection at 5 times magnification.
After each N-045 exposure, end-to-end conductor resistance shall be no more than 10 percent above its pre-test value.
After each N-045 exposure, conductor-to-conductor and conductor-to-case insulation resistance shall be at least 1 megohm at 50 V DC.
Powered electronics shall retain operational functions throughout the N-046 exposure.
Battery temperatures shall remain within manufacturer operating limits throughout the N-046 exposure.
Battery charging shall remain inhibited whenever measured battery temperature is outside the manufacturer permitted charge range.
The vessel shall self-right within 60 seconds of each N-051 release.

The vessel shall retain its ballast through every N-051 release.

Within 5 minutes of each N-054 snag, full commanded rudder travel shall be regained.

The vessel shall enter fouling-contingency state within 10 seconds after the N-055 trigger.

Mean water-relative powered speed through each N-056 patch passage shall be at least 50 percent of weed-free reference speed.
Motor and controller currents shall remain within their respective rated limits during each N-056 patch passage.
Motor and controller temperatures shall remain within their respective rated limits during each N-056 patch passage.
A locked propulsor shall cause motor shutdown within 2 seconds.
Motor thrust shall remain disabled whenever an attempt is qualifying or qualification status is unknown.
After restart, motor enable shall remain inhibited until recovery is authorized by the onboard safety function or a fresh authenticated operator command.
In the E-006 injection test, an ingress event record shall exist within 60 seconds of injection starting.
Within 30 seconds after a watchdog reset under E-003 preconditions, qualification status shall equal the valid persisted status, or be nonqualifying when persisted status is absent or inconsistent.
The installed energy architecture shall support the selected bounded repeating profile without external charging, meeting the derived reserve, cycle-balance and peak-supply criteria.

The hull shall remain within its validated functional deformation limit under the applicable load cases.

Each hull skin panel shall remain within its validated functional deformation limit under the applicable load cases.

Stiffness credited in structural qualification shall not exceed the qualified wet-conditioned production-laminate bounds.

TransGorgeCourse defines nominal marker references and directed finite gate segments. Completion has no elapsed-time deadline. Position history must demonstrate crossings; touching a gate line alone does not count.

Passive live monitoring and autonomous polling of weather services are permitted. Any operator-supplied update, remote emergency abort or manual control ends qualification. Weather data must be obtained by the system without manual operator submission.
An auxiliary motor may remain installed. Motor use is permitted during separate development tests and vessel recovery; use during an attempt ends its qualification.
Monitoring-link loss shall not interrupt autonomous mission execution. Retained telemetry shall be transmitted after contact returns.
Use disqualifies the attempt as unassisted.

Evaluate the actual encounter and visibility conditions, including lookout, collision-risk assessment, avoidance action, safe speed, overtaking, sailing encounters and narrow-channel obligations. A safety action takes precedence over preserving attempt qualification.
Include dam restricted areas, lock approaches excluded by the challenge, and applicable temporary safety/security zones or closures. Use the chart and notice set applicable to the attempt.

The operating context includes commercial tows, passenger vessels, fishing craft, recreational powerboats, sailing vessels and people in the water. Channel non-impediment and encounter conduct remain independently required by C-007. The vehicle analysis defines representative and adverse traffic scenarios and assesses maneuver feasibility.
Measure maximum fore-and-aft extent, including rudders, rig projections, antennas and other equipment, across normal operating configurations. Hull arrangement is unrestricted.
A demonstrated backup preserving the function permits continuation. Darkness alone is not a fault. Fog triggers this rule when it compromises required capability.
Do not wait for operator intervention or communications. Select a viable route based on remaining capabilities. Intentional grounding at a suitable accessible shore is permitted.
Queue the alert while communications are unavailable and transmit when contact returns.
Apply flotation, retention and post-capsize recovery obligations C-016 through C-018.
Demonstrate in the declared casualty qualification conditions for the interval needed to execute shore recovery.
Use the same casualty qualification conditions as C-016.
Self-righting is not prescribed; inverted recovery is permitted. Auxiliary propulsion ends qualification. Demonstrate against declared course recovery conditions.
Grounding, anchoring, attaching to shore or entering designated refuge ends qualification. Safe waiting under sail is permitted and counts toward elapsed exposure.
Continue navigation and retain telemetry onboard; replay retained data after reconnection.
Use the declared mission configuration and forecast-conditioned scenarios. No fixed completion deadline applies.
Forecast applicability must cover remaining passage and recovery options; assess against observations.
Account for adverse current, essential onboard loads and uncertainty along the recovery route. No fixed motor-runtime reserve is substituted for route analysis.
Include the decision and maneuver margin needed to enter recovery.
Required navigation, traffic safety and observation functions remain applicable. Nightfall alone does not require refuge.
No autonomous resumption from refuge. Operator-commanded relocation is permitted outside qualification.
Allocate indications consistently with applicable navigation signals; no light or sound configuration is prescribed here.

C-000 defines the governing finite challenge obligations. Course review, unassisted sail-only operation, safety capability, recovery reserve and the persistent attempt state apply throughout. Safe unassisted righting may preserve qualification; motor propulsion, external intervention or required safety-capability loss ends it.

N-010 operational functions and applicable N-001 shared conditions apply. The mission history includes sailing, maneuvers and holds until completion. Conservative usable energy must remain above the R-002 reserve. No fixed duration or nonnegative daily energy balance is required.
Energy estimation and conservative decision inputs; accuracy uses calibrated energy integration across operating battery temperatures.

Qualification uses the selected mission profile. Accuracy trials contain 1800 scheduled one-second epochs in 30 minutes; invalid or missing epochs count as failed epochs. Position and heading criteria use the same set of at least 1710 qualifying epochs, preventing separate selection of different good samples. Fault-injection runs are separate.
Watchdog-reset tests start above protected reserve with valid navigation observations. Normal sailing remains subject to N-035; data and qualification persistence have shared leaf criteria.
Reserve means R-002. Emergency/recovery cadence takes precedence; clearing low-energy state is independent of other modes, while payload enabling respects all restrictions.

Link availability is a delivery-test precondition, not a coverage guarantee. Normal, low-energy and recovery delivery cadence is 30 seconds, as allocated by GorgeChallenge::liveObservation. Outage tests last 24 hours.
All leaves use a 30-minute freshwater injection at 10 mL/min into the normally dry hull. No pump technology is prescribed; R-004 remains applicable.

Periodic records contain position, heading, mode, gate progress, battery energy and fault state. Critical events are independent of periodic cadence. Timestamp accuracy is assessed with valid GNSS time.
Demonstrate with one adult, no powered lift, a firm bank or ramp of slope at most 1:12, wind at most 5 m/s and waves at most 0.2 m. This is not a survival-envelope recovery claim.
Every printed component must be producible as one or more such jobs. The envelope includes the selected build orientation, supports, brim, raft and printer-required clearance.
Exercise individual replacement of the battery, every electronics module, every actuator and every serviceable enclosure seal by one operator using hand tools.

Use independently recorded head-on, crossing and overtaking AIS and non-AIS targets, day and night in the selected operational profile. Allocations shall include kinematic response distance, uncertainty, consequence-informed clearance and margins, and required timely observation and whole-response reliability with confidence criteria. Unreliably classified targets shall use a reviewed conservative envelope spanning plausible classes and occupant transitions. Collision avoidance and nonimpediment obligations remain unchanged.

Use uploaded permitted-water and exclusion polygons, with a 60-second prediction horizon. Inject approaches to every boundary, navigation loss and no-feasible-maneuver cases. Coordinates and uncertainty/clearance margins are controlled mission inputs with no default values.
Emergency intervention ends attempt qualification. Exercise active emergency, powered recovery, local isolation and remote-control loss, including coexisting low-energy flags.

Use the deployment-specific compliance matrix for sailing, powered-recovery and stationary modes, including its visibility, arcs, colors and sound criteria. The matrix remains a deployment hold point under S-005.
Acceptance is deployment document review, not onboard behavior or an assertion of buoy status.

Gorge qualification uses N-010; ocean qualification uses N-020. Both include applicable shared exposure requirements. Operational functions are navigation, sail/steering control, recording and available-link telemetry. Survival requires flotation, attached rig/ballast, dry electronics and retained mission state; course progress is not required. Required traffic assessment, navigation signals and available-link location reporting remain safety obligations in every mode. Loss of required safety capability invokes C-012 even when the structure survives.
Gorge uses N-041 freshwater exposure; ocean uses N-042 saltwater exposure; dual-profile qualification requires both. Shared sealing, material-aging and thermal checks use the selected campaign.

Capsize and vegetation are separate disturbance cases. Righting and upright control restoration apply to the selected N-051 strategy; C-018 also permits post-abort limp recovery. Weed passage, snag shedding and blockage response apply to the declared Gorge exposure. No disturbance waives required safety capability or motor inhibition.

Use route-specific wind, waves, current and casualty state, with installed propulsion performance. R-004 governs motor enable and challenge qualification; S-003 governs isolation and control loss. Course recovery scenarios must be accepted before qualification.

Route evaluation supplies powered and essential durations from current position to a suitable retrieval location, including adverse current and final approach. Essential duration includes all powered transit. Powers use the installed configuration; uncertaintyFactor is at least one. An unavailable or infeasible recovery route cannot produce a valid reserve.

Freshness threshold is 120 seconds for normal, emergency, powered recovery or unknown mode, and 600 seconds only for explicitly reported low energy without emergency or powered recovery. Staleness describes data age, not diagnosed link failure. Exercise a 24-hour outage and reconnection.
Exercise complete command receipt, authentication failure, replayed sequence numbers, age greater than 30 seconds, and external control during a qualifying attempt.
Gorge-specific parameter limits and applicable shared exposure requirements apply together.
Ocean-specific parameter limits and applicable shared exposure requirements apply together.
Operational functions are defined by N-001. Mean wind uses a 10-minute average referenced to 10 m above water.
N-001 defines operational functions. Wave statistics use 20-minute records.

Use N-001 survival outcomes and the operational wind reference convention. Selected-profile wave, current, temperature and humidity limits apply concurrently. BlueDogEnvironmentReview::RecoveryExposureHours includes casualty transit and declared pickup delay.
Operational functions are defined by N-001. Mean wind uses a 10-minute average referenced to 10 m above water.
N-001 defines operational functions. Wave statistics use 20-minute records.
Use N-001 survival outcomes and the operational wind reference convention. Selected-profile wave, current, temperature and humidity limits apply concurrently.
N-001/N-035 define operational and survival functions.
N-001/N-035 define operational and survival functions.

Exercise daylight and darkness at meteorological visibility of at least 1 km, and detected visibility below 1 km. Apply current BlueDogClassDetection class-specific or conservative plausible-class envelopes and the S-001 reviewed observation and response criteria.

Calm-mode functions are navigation, recording and autonomous boundary/traffic contingency. Waiting may continue only while forecast coverage, traffic/boundary safety and measured calm-mode loads preserve route-dependent recovery authority; no fixed waiting endurance is imposed. Autonomous safety recovery first terminates qualification under GorgeChallenge::safetyCapabilityAbort, then may enable the motor under R-004.

The trigger is a detected upper operational wind or wave limit exceedance for the selected profile; calm invokes N-034. Resumption eligibility requires 10 continuous minutes inside the selected wind/wave limits, valid navigation, upright control, preserved required safety capability and no low-energy, emergency-recovery or isolation restriction. Resuming a control mode never clears a disqualified attempt.
Evaluate after each selected profile wet-exposure campaign under N-002.
Evaluate disconnected cable assemblies after each selected profile wet-exposure campaign under N-002; disconnect electronics for insulation measurement.
Expose the powered vessel to 40 degC ambient air and 1000 W/m2 incident solar irradiance for 8 hours; use the installed battery manufacturer temperature limits.

Use exposure representative of the selected mission and intended service interval, followed by N-041 for Gorge or N-042 for ocean. Establish aged directional load bounds for the actual print and joints. Inspect and measure the maximum fore-and-aft extent through all normal rig, steering and equipment configurations. Apply the executable lengthLimit constraint with recorded measurement uncertainty; confirm no unmeasured projection extends beyond the reported envelope.

Inject loss of required safety functions, including visibility-driven loss and common-cause faults. Confirm qualification terminates when the function is unavailable; demonstrate continued qualification only when an accepted backup maintains that function.

From declared course locations and casualty states, remove communications and trigger safety abort. Record recovery initiation, chosen accessible destination, transit and final approach. Assess impaired-sensing collision exposure and consequences independently; a successful transit alone does not accept that residual risk.

Trigger abort with available and unavailable links. Observe immediate transmission attempts with a link, durable queueing without a link and delivery after reconnection. Timing implementation tolerance must be declared before qualification.
Review and demonstrate the linked flotation, major-component retention and capsize recovery cases using the same casualty configuration. Account for every major component at retrieval.

Execute the approved flooding and capsize exposure cases with maximum mission load. Observe flotation throughout the course-derived recovery duration. A short static float test cannot substantiate a longer recovery exposure.
Inspect rig, ballast and battery retention before and after the same flooding and capsize cases used for flotation. Record attachments and any released debris.

Release the vessel in the declared capsize orientations with communications disabled and execute shore recovery under the approved current, wind and wave profile. Observe arrival at a retrievable location; remaining inverted is allowed. Motor use must disqualify the attempt.

Review timestamped passage records and inject grounding, anchoring, shore attachment and refuge entry. Each ends qualification; safe afloat waiting does not. Missing evidence prevents an affirmative qualification verdict.

Interrupt communications during healthy passage and verify continued autonomous operation, retained observations and backlog delivery. Separately inject a safety failure during the outage to ensure loss of contact does not inhibit recovery.

Exercise forecast-conditioned launch scenarios covering full passage, waiting and recovery exposure. Reject missing or insufficient forecast coverage. Evaluate the frozen Monte Carlo ensemble and explicit edge cases without treating sample completion fraction as calibrated real-world probability.

Interrupt weather access with applicable and expired forecasts; independently vary onboard safety capability. Confirm continuation requires both applicable forecast information and preserved safety capability.

Evaluate route-dependent reserve along the course using installed load evidence, adverse currents, route feasibility and uncertainty. An inaccessible shore, infeasible route or missing input cannot establish a protected reserve.

Inject declining energy and increasing recovery demand along the route. Confirm recovery begins with sufficient reserve for the decision delay, transition and transit rather than only after reserve exhaustion.

Exercise the declared navigation, traffic, communications and recovery scenarios in darkness. Confirm nightfall alone does not terminate qualification. Simulation cannot close optical sensing or navigation-light physical evidence.

After abort, test reboot, contact restoration, refuge departure and operator relocation. Qualification remains ended until the new attempt departure-gate condition is met; partial progress is not carried forward.
Inspect and test recovery indications against the deployment-specific navigation-signal matrix in the approved visibility conditions, including the casualty states for which recovery is claimed.

A component nameplate or summed nominal power does not establish installed peak delivery.
